node.label: Michelle Perrot
node.date_label: Les ouvriers en grève (1974; catalogued also as 1973) · L’Impossible prison (1980) · Une histoire des femmes est-elle possible ? (1984) · Histoire de la vie privée IV (1987) · Histoire des femmes en Occident, with Georges Duby (1991–1992) · Les femmes ou les silences de l’histoire (1998) · Histoire de chambres (2009)
node.description: Les femmes ou les silences de l’histoire (1998) investigates how women were silenced in archives and historical narratives, and how traces of their work, private lives and political action can be recovered. Its inquiry moves from recovering women’s activities to examining relations between the sexes and the making of historical evidence. Yannick Ripa praised its gathering and recontextualization of dispersed essays, while wishing Perrot had developed her observation that the field’s problematic remained hesitant. Perrot’s earlier Les ouvriers en grève combines statistical analysis with workers’ collective lives; Robert Brécy praised the study but argued that, perhaps under the influence of May 1968, it stressed the festive side of strikes when their marches and meetings answered first to the necessities of struggle. With Georges Duby she co-directed Histoire des femmes en Occident (1991–1992), a collective enterprise that made new research on women’s history in Western universities visible. Histoire de chambres (2009) connects rooms, intimacy and enclosure; Alain Corbin praised the synthesis while suggesting that changes within rural houses received overly brief treatment.

node.scope_note: Monographs, edited volumes and thesis unread in full. The 1998 collection, strike book and 2009 rooms book are characterized through named reviewers Ripa, Brécy and Corbin. The 1980 and 2023 interviews are read directly; formation and seminar links use retrospective biographical or reported evidence. The 2002 and 2010 interviews and Scott’s 2017 contribution remain unread. Written institutional interview presentation read; audio unheard.

proposed_edges.relationship: Labrousse supervised Perrot’s strike-history thesis (1971), published as Les ouvriers en grève (1974); she combined his serial methods with attention to workers’ speech and gestures.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Lacoue-Labarthe (2015), L’histoire du monde ouvrier, paragraphs beginning L’approche méthodologique and Si Michelle Perrot: “sous sa direction”; distinguishes thesis from book. Thesis and book unread; retrospective formation evidence.

proposed_edges.relationship: Perrot and Duby co-directed the five-volume French Histoire des femmes en Occident (1991–1992).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Institut de France (2009), opening presentation and bibliography: five volumes, co-direction, 1991–1992; written text read, audio unheard and volumes unread. BnF (2025), pp. 5–6, distinguishes series directors from volume editors. Existing edge_442 joins Duby to women, not these two people.

proposed_edges.relationship: Perrot organized discussion with Foucault of Surveiller et punir (1975) in the collective L’Impossible prison (1980).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Fabre interview (1980), p. 6, first answer: “engager une discussion”; identifies Léonard’s paper, Foucault’s reply and the round table. Both interview pages read; collected papers unread. Exchange does not imply agreement on every argument.

proposed_edges.relationship: Perrot and Farge co-led the women’s-history reading seminar from 1978–1979 that helped assemble the team behind Histoire des femmes en Occident (1991–1992).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Lacoue-Labarthe, Dictionnaire des féministes (2017), paragraph beginning De même, à partir de 1978-1979: “co-anime”; APHG report (2026), paragraph beginning Dans la suite de sa carrière, independently names Farge in the reading group. Seminar papers and volumes unread; series and volume editorships are not conflated.

proposed_edges.relationship: According to Isabelle Lacoue-Labarthe (2017), Perrot adopted gender as an analytical tool theorised by Scott; Ripa’s review of Les femmes ou les silences de l’histoire (1998) likewise presents her examination of employers’, unions’ and political-economic discourse on women’s work as following Scott.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Lacoue-Labarthe’s signed dictionary entry (2017), paragraph beginning “Si elle adopte”, explicitly associates Perrot’s analytical use of gender with Scott’s theorisation, dated there to 1988. Ripa (1999), p. 147, opening paragraph, independently describes her analysis of three discourses as following Scott. Both are mediated witnesses; the Perrot and Scott originals remain unread. Preserve counts_toward_floor false pending coordinator review of the strengthened evidence.
proposed_edges.map_label: Scott’s analytical gender and labour discourse

proposed_edges.relationship: Perrot says that Beauvoir’s Le Deuxième Sexe (1949) shaped her life and first impulse to research feminism, in her 2023 interview with Florent Le Bot.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: L’OURS (2023), answers to 1949, Le deuxième sexe: initial extracts, fuller reading in 1954–1955, then “orienté mon premier élan de recherches”. Complete interview read; Beauvoir’s book unread here. Influence distinguished from Perrot’s later active feminism.

proposed_edges.relationship: Lacoue-Labarthe places Perrot’s turn toward history from below in the wake of Thompson’s The Making of the English Working Class (1963).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Lacoue-Labarthe (2015), L’histoire du monde ouvrier, paragraph beginning Aux côtés de l’initiateur: “dans le sillage”. Scholarly biographer’s characterization; no direct Perrot testimony or date of first reading established. Thompson’s book unread here.
proposed_edges.map_label: Thompson as a retrospectively identified resource

proposed_edges.relationship: In his review of Histoire de chambres (2009), Corbin praises Perrot’s synthesis but suggests that the partitioning of rural houses into private rooms receives overly brief treatment.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Corbin (2009), Espèces d’espaces, final paragraph beginning Le processus qui conduit: “un peu trop rapidement, peut-être”. Full review and notes read; Perrot’s book unread. A local reservation within an appreciative review, not wholesale rejection.
proposed_edges.map_label: Corbin’s qualified reservation on rural rooms

proposed_edges.relationship: Les femmes ou les silences de l’histoire (1998) investigates women’s uneven survival in historical records and recovers their work, private lives and political action, as Ripa’s review explains.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Ripa (1999), pp. 145–147, especially p. 146 on archival selection, private papers and the collection’s organization. Review read, book unread; claim is mediated through this named reader. Existing women roster row records volume editorship, not a person-node edge.
proposed_edges.map_label: Recovering women and interrogating historical silences

proposed_edges.relationship: In Brécy’s reading, Les ouvriers en grève (1974) shifts labour history toward strike action and workers’ lives while combining statistical series with qualitative analysis.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Brécy (1976), pp. 115–116: opening contrasts institutions with strikes; p. 115 discusses statistics and psychology; p. 116 details collective life and criticizes festive emphasis. Complete review read, book unread. Its 1974 dating differs from BnF’s 1973; see chronology.

proposed_edges.relationship: In Les femmes ou les silences de l’histoire (1998), Perrot uses relations between the sexes to re-examine women’s work and exclusion from citizenship, as Ripa’s review describes.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Ripa (1999), end p. 146 and first half p. 147, moves from description of women’s activities to discourse and civic exclusion; dictionary (2017), paragraph beginning Si elle adopte, independently identifies gender as an analytical tool. Book unread; no replacement of women’s history asserted.

proposed_edges.relationship: In L’immigration en France, une histoire en friche (1986), Gérard Noiriel draws on Perrot’s Les rapports entre ouvriers français et étrangers (1871–1893) (1960) to explain how hostility toward immigrant workers helped crystallize nationalism among French workers.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read Persée’s page-specific article text on pp. 760–765 and the references on p. 767. Noiriel names Perrot in the body and quotes her explanation of nationalism, then develops the relationship between immigration and labour politics. This is substantive uptake, not an isolated bibliographic citation. Her 1960 article itself was not read; the claim concerns Noiriel’s use of it.
proposed_edges.map_label: Worker xenophobia and the crystallization of nationalism

proposed_edges.relationship: In Différences entre les sexes et domination symbolique (1993), Roger Chartier questions the conventional periodization retained in Perrot and Duby’s Histoire des femmes en Occident (1991–1992), while acknowledging its legitimacy for a project examining how broader historical changes affected relations between the sexes.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read the complete six-page note through Persée’s page-specific HTML, pp. 1005–1010. Although its bibliographic heading identifies volume III (1991), the periodization passage expressly discusses all five volumes. The criticism concerns the co-directed enterprise, not solely Perrot’s individual writing. It includes Chartier’s qualification rather than presenting him as simply rejecting the project. The volumes themselves were not read.
proposed_edges.map_label: Questioning conventional periods in women’s history

proposed_edges.relationship: Perrot’s Les ouvriers en grève. France, 1871–1890 (1974) contributes to quantitative history by combining measurement of strike activity with close analysis of manuscript and printed evidence, a methodological combination emphasized by Gabriel Désert’s review (1976).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read the opening page directly in Persée’s HTML. Désert identifies the quantitative method and its combination with extensive documentary analysis, then discusses the regional distribution of strikes and strikers. This records a specific methodological contribution, without claiming that Perrot founded the approach. The remaining review pages and the monograph were not read. The year follows this contemporary review; the original packet notes bibliographic variation between 1973 and 1974.
proposed_edges.map_label: Combining strike statistics with documentary analysis

proposed_edges.relationship: In Histoire de chambres (2009), Perrot historicizes the bedroom as a distinct space within the dwelling, connecting the specialization of rooms with experiences of privacy and enclosure, as Alain Corbin’s review explains.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read Corbin’s substantive review on the journal’s own site. It distinguishes the room’s spatial organization from the experiences it permits and details the progressive specialization of rooms. Mapping this contribution to spatialhistory is an editorial classification, not a claim that Perrot founded a school. The monograph was not read. Reuses the packet’s source mp_w_corbin_2009; no additional Perrot–Corbin pair is proposed.
